findings.title: Portable operation extension and GPU-result contracts need a concrete minimum catalog
findings.problem: The new call! entry correctly rejects unknown functions, but mul!/Array examples do not specify the public way a library defines a retained/reselectable operation, nor complete result/shape contracts for reductions and allocations. A CPU future from a scalar-returning operation cannot simply be a GPU loop predicate. Raw kernels can implement these workloads; clean reusable operation-layer coverage is not yet established.
findings.required_resolution: Document the portable extension hook/recipe contract and a minimum supported-family matrix covering effects, result identity/type, deferred shapes, workspace, control eligibility and invalidation. Include GPU-output reductions/convergence storage, plus allocating/view results with device-written shapes. Reuse the existing operation definitions; do not add device/group adaptation or infer returns from !.
acceptance: Known GPU-output reduction drives two nested loop invocations without host readback; scalar CPU-result form is explicitly distinguished.
A package-defined portable operation uses one numerical body, retains a reselectable recipe and discovers captured resources; unsupported functions reject before submission.
Unqualified allocating/view variants reject; any additional qualified definition states initial dimensions, metadata-readiness/lifetime, bounded capacity and stable output identity before/after run.
text_clarification_applied: Minimum recorded signature/return/effect catalog added in api.md.
GPU-resident mapped sum uses existing Base.sum!(f,r,A) with a one-element ordinary device array destination; no new public scalar result type or dot! API.
Current GPUArrays in-place reductions already have this interface but eager isempty/Array(r) empty paths cannot run during graph construction for GPU-written lengths.

Portable definition boundary is specified by ordinary call! Julia dispatch/shared recipes. Generic allocating/metadata-only families are not in the required catalog and must reject until their result/shape/lifetime contracts are supplied; native implementation qualification remains open.

Library composition/extension boundary now uses ordinary call! frontend Julia dispatch plus one private shared definition/retained recipe; operand types participate in recipe lookup. No generic capture/registry or whole-builder adapter.

findings.title: DNN emitter temporary/output lifetimes must be mapped explicitly
findings.problem: DNNKernels currently returns unbound module outputs, including views, as owner-graph temporaries for subsequent caller nodes. A mechanical switch to persistent-default constructors makes all intermediates persistent and defeats arena reuse; prohibiting any returned scratch handle would instead break same-graph composition. GPU-written scratch size metadata is arena-local too and cannot be host-read after the run.
findings.required_resolution: Produce an emitter allocation/escape map: internal scratch, same-owner graph-only outputs/views, and persistent outputs saved/shared beyond a run. Clarify that returning a scratch handle for further owner-graph declarations is legal; using its data or arena metadata outside its run is not. This clarification requires no new array type or adaptation.
acceptance: Two modules share a scratch view within one graph and match the independent numerical reference; arena liveness includes its root.
A retained result used by graph two is explicitly persistent or copied; internal workspace remains scratch and is reclaimed/aliased.
Host queries never read GPU-written scratch metadata from reused arena bytes.
text_clarification_applied: docs/api.md now permits returning scratch handles for further owner-run declarations; this does not permit data escape.
Host reads of GPU-written scratch metadata outside the owner run explicitly reject.

Concrete make/scratch/activation/weights/bound/view/recurrent/noise allocation map added in execution-contracts §16.12, including removal of the zero-size persistent-resource workaround; actual port/native composition gates remain open.

findings.title: One-shot readback requests are easy to consume during warmup or reuse stale across runs
findings.problem: call!(g,Array,a) returns a future for the next execution. Warmup/seed runs can consume that request, and repeated fetch must intentionally keep returning its original snapshot. Reusing the same future in a token/frame loop therefore does not mean latest result. The API can express fresh requests through Readback(previous), but the concrete consumer protocol and retention bounds need qualification.
findings.required_resolution: Specify a canonical warmup/production replay request protocol: bind after warmup, request before each desired execution, preserve old snapshots, and have a new request retain only the stable output descriptor rather than a chain of previous future payloads. Do not silently redefine fetch as latest-value access or introduce another eager future mode.
acceptance: Warmup then multiple production runs returns the intended token/frame for each request; an old future still returns its original value.
Pending requests survive compatible growth/recompile; output deletion/free rejects unsubmitted requests.
Dropping prior futures gives bounded staging/CPU storage; retained snapshots remain immutable under replay.
findings.needed_before: B2/B3 output lifecycle and B5 consumers
text_clarification_applied: Canonical sequence consumes initial request during first warmup and rearms before each wanted production execution; no implicit persistent-state reset.
Readback(previous) retains stable output descriptor only; completed requests leave Graph pending set and are not retained as a history.
Live results plus bounded staging cache define memory bound; native lifecycle/memory qualification remains open.

findings.title: Sparse/block-sparse and matrix-free operator support is named but not specified
findings.problem: The plan promises sparse conversion and SpMV/FEM solves without defining their supported composite layouts and operation contracts. The AScanner snapshot has block-COO values/row/column buffers with a common live triplet count and one-based block indices; ge2sym! publishes a GPU selection count. PrintSim also uses matrix-free products/preconditioners. Dense mul! and independent per-array resizing are insufficient evidence for these composite semantics.
findings.required_resolution: Specify compatible sparse/block layouts, logical index base/width, duplicate accumulation/symmetry semantics, coherent multi-array GPU counts, resource discovery, and the matrix-free/preconditioner extension boundary. Choose portable/shared operation definitions with capability-selected candidates, not one numerical API per backend. Existing upstream composites may wrap MantleArrays; no new public array family is implied.
acceptance: COO/block-COO select/sort/combine -> sparse product -> convergence agrees with an independent tiny CPU system at zero/nonzero nnz.
Rows/columns/values use the same logical count and poisoned tails never participate.
Matrix-free and assembled products plus preconditioned convergence agree at required precision; unsupported FP64/atomic semantics reject rather than silently weaken.
findings.needed_before: B2 sparse/operator catalog and B5 FEM/particle gates
text_clarification_applied: §16.12 specifies sparse schema requirements, coherent values/rows/cols count publication, duplicate/symmetry/index checks, pattern/value invalidation and matrix-free mul!/ldiv! qualified-definition boundaries. No new array family or per-backend sparse policy.

findings.title: Window capture and picking need one explicit frame-consistency contract
findings.problem: Array(window) still means the next presented frame, unlike eager Array(image), and the supported recorded Array(window) path is not explicitly defined. RayMakie retains picking metadata plus its plot map/extent; returning correct pixel bytes with a newer plot map can select the wrong object. Headless image smoke does not qualify acquire/copy/present/generation behavior or a small picking read.
findings.required_resolution: Specify the supported window/offscreen snapshot route and timing, capture before presentation, generation/extent ownership, and how the consumer associates immutable frame plot maps with the matching snapshot. Qualify small ROI/pixel readback without requiring full-frame downloads. Do not guess a presenting graph from an array or add a backend-specific screenshot path. Include CPU pixel layout/orientation and color/metadata decoding so the native storage representation never leaks into per-backend consumer code.
acceptance: Onscreen/offscreen readback and picking identify the correct frame/plot after resize or plot removal while an earlier request is pending.
No missing next-frame deadlock in a synchronous colorbuffer path; failures/skips/close wake requests.
Window/present lifetime is independently qualified; small picking reads avoid full-image transfers.
text_clarification_applied: Explicit call!(presenting_graph,Array,win) snapshots the acquired frame before present; Array(win) rejects to avoid waiting for unsubmitted future work. Supersedes old next-present blocking proposal.
Color/ID/depth captures retain the same frame map/extent/format/pixel scale; ROI uses region copy/device extraction and the common output protocol. Actual WSI/native profiles stay open.

findings.title: Nested solver/control migration needs realistic cost and predicate-boundary checks
findings.problem: PrintSim launch!/is_recording currently recognize Graph, not Group; is_recording(target)=target isa Mantle.Graph. Updating only the launch dispatch can leave Group emission taking the immediate solver branch and host-reading a convergence flag before graph execution. PrintSim uses device-side CG flags, sequential line-search loops, per-dispatch ConditionalTarget predicates and optional CPU diagnostics; a whole Group predicate is sampled once, so predicates cannot be collapsed blindly. The fixed scaling MWE covers a long single loop, not realistic nested expansion. Hikari already documents per-sample allocations from abstract/Any plan-holder boundaries.
findings.required_resolution: Generalize Graph-only emitter signatures/classification to explicit Graph/Group emission without routing through a device/array adapter. Map original predicate sampling/reset points to explicit regions/individual conditionals; retain pure GPU and explicit diagnostic host modes separately. Add actual nested native/portable plan-size, stopped-work and compile/runtime measurements using the existing MWE profiles. Keep consumer session/graph holders concretely typed or behind measured function barriers; no new backend runtime. PrintSim timestep/configuration dependencies also require explicit handling: a changed dt can invalidate FEM/coarse setup even if array shapes do not change; updating a GPURef alone is insufficient.
acceptance: The same solver emission into Graph and Group takes the recorded path, never host-reads convergence during construction and discovers identical resource effects.
Nested Newton -> CG and line search preserve state/reset and active-versus-stopped effects, including a flag changed within a larger phase.
GPU-only path has no scalar host readback; explicit CPU diagnostics occur at documented host boundaries.
Report nested fallback expansion/slot bytes and post-stop work before claiming efficient FEM/decode on hardware lacking native loops; unchanged replay/session dispatch has no unexplained boxing.
Changing a timestep-dependent configuration rebuilds/recomputes the required operator/coarse data or rejects clearly; persistent simulation state is not silently reset.
text_clarification_applied: §16.12 specifies Group-aware recording classification, sibling/lexical solver control, realistic nested-control costs, explicit host diagnostic mode and dt-dependent setup recompute/reject.

findings.title: Contiguous KV growth is not paged-attention/continuous-batching coverage
findings.problem: Bonsai kv_page rounds growth of contiguous Int8 K/V and Float32 scale arrays; it does not demonstrate a GPU page table, page reuse or per-request ownership. The plan names paged access but provides no corresponding layout/membership/lifetime qualification. Core span refinement on ordinary strided views alone is not proof of non-affine page-table access or useful overlap.

evidence.symbol: ### 16.6 Imported allocations and explicit device communication

findings.required_resolution: Either explicitly bound the initial LLM gate to contiguous packed caches, or specify the shared paged-layout/resource-set and page reuse/lease contract plus a real paged attention case. Preserve tracked reachable resources, quantized scale relationships and safe multi-session page retirement. Hardware-specific optimized candidates remain behind shared capability dispatch. Logical attention paging is a data/layout contract and need not require hardware sparse residency.
acceptance: A shuffled page mapping matches contiguous/reference attention for two sessions sharing weights.
Reassign a page only after all old readers finish; stale descriptors/scale mappings cannot address reused storage.
Measure useful append/read/upload overlap and conservative-hazard costs; contiguous capacity doubling does not close this gate.
text_clarification_applied: Contiguous cache is the initial gate; logical paged cache is library-owned ordinary arrays/page-table/scales with qualified attention definitions, common root/span ordering and page leases. Shuffled-page/continuous-batching runtime/performance profile remains open.

findings.title: Training needs an explicit AD boundary and activation lifetime test
findings.problem: The plan correctly puts AD algorithms outside Mantle but does not say where differentiation happens relative to call!/materialization/run!. Differentiating eager model code, differentiating a graph builder and emitting an already differentiated program are different integrations. Inference and a standalone optimizer kernel do not validate backward saved values, mutation/alias versions or scratch lifetime.
findings.required_resolution: State the supported external AD/emitter boundary and what operation identity/effect/result metadata it consumes. Saved activations must remain in one owner run or use explicit persistent storage between forward/backward runs; external AD owns mathematical versioning/checkpoint/recompute choices. No generic AD-through-call! promise follows from the common array interface.
acceptance: A tiny independently checked forward/backward/optimizer step replays with correct gradients and persistent optimizer/RNG state.
Saved view/alias data survives through backward; cross-run saved values do not retain arena scratch accidentally.
Finite-difference/reference comparison and memory/timing distinguish real training from inference.
text_clarification_applied: §16.12 places AD before forward/backward emission or in numerical-function rules; differentiating runtime graph bookkeeping is not promised. Same-run saved activations may be scratch; cross-run state is persistent with version/reader ordering. Actual external-AD/reference qualification remains open.

alias_header_ruling.problem: One physical allocation can have independent differently shaped/typed foreign headers. Canonical payload identity cannot imply one logical dimensions/capacity cell or element unit.
alias_header_ruling.decision: One shared allocation/byte hazard and ownership identity; distinct logical-header metadata unless aliases deliberately share a logical parent. Checked typed byte spans at descriptor publication. No vendor shape mutation or readonly/lease bypass.
alias_header_ruling.qualification: Existing MWE-07, no additional family; imported buffers remain nonrelocatable and source facts must qualify their bounds/identity.
alias_header_ruling.interop_checkpoint: A new foreign import captures supplied header geometry; existing Mantle wrapper reuse shares its GPU size. Export to a concrete vendor header may require a coherent metadata checkpoint outside locks and matching storage lease. Arbitrary vendor callbacks are conservatively read/write; readonly requires qualified effects.
